top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-59 symlink hardlink link-following symbolic-link file-link archive-extraction path-resolution file-overwrite race filesystem
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject unsafe links and verify resolved file targets before access.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
top_sast_rules.description: Creating a temporary file that is accessible by other users can lead to information disclosure and sometimes remote code execution.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-378. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
top_sast_rules.description: External links that open in a new tab or window but do not specify link type 'noopener' or 'noreferrer' are a potential security risk.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Find code that may expose sensitive information in error messages, logs, or responses
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper access controls and avoid exposing sensitive information in responses, errors, or logs.

top_sast_rules.description: If two functions with the same name are declared in the same scope, one of the declarations overrides the other without warning. This makes the code hard to read and maintain, and may even lead to platform-dependent behavior.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove unused variables that may contain sensitive data. Use static analysis tools to identify unused code. Review code for potential logic errors.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to this vulnerability type. Review the query logic for detailed requirements.

top_sast_rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-425 forced-browsing direct-request restricted-url protected-route protected-file missing-authorization route endpoint hidden-link
top_sast_rules.remediation: Authorize every protected route and resource on direct access.

top_sast_rules.description: Passing identical, or seemingly identical, operands to an operator such as subtraction or conjunction may indicate a typo; even if it is intentional, it makes the code hard to read.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove dead code through static analysis. Use code coverage tools to identify unreachable code. Implement regular code reviews to eliminate unused functionality.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
top_sast_rules.description: Using externally controlled strings to construct HTML might allow a malicious user to perform a cross-site scripting attack.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Detect output operations that lack proper encoding for the target context
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use context-appropriate encoding for all output operations. Implement proper escaping for HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and URL contexts.

top_sast_rules.description: Legacy category for insecure credential creation, storage, validation, or handling.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-255 credential-management password token secret credential storage rotation validation authentication-secret
top_sast_rules.remediation: Protect credentials throughout storage, validation, transport, and rotation.
